title: Vanishing of higher direct images for retrocompact opens in local dimension at most one
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] such that every local ring $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and has ring Krull dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subset which is retrocompact, meaning that $U\cap V$ is quasi-compact for every quasi-compact open $V\subseteq X$ (quasi-compactness as in [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme]). Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion of the open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. For every quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent] and every integer $p>0$, the higher direct image $R^pj_*\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-cohomology] is zero.

source.place: Tag 09N8, label lemma-affine, statement at lines 7747-7752; used in Tag 09N9, label lemma-open-in-affine-curve-affine

proof.text: Retrocompactness makes U.ι quasi-compact: for any affine open V of X, the image of its inverse image under the open embedding U.ι is U ∩ V, compact by retrocompactness. An open immersion is quasi-separated. To prove that G = R^p(U.ι)_*F is zero, apply stalkwise detection of zero objects to its underlying abelian sheaf, and reflect zero through the faithful forgetful functor from modules.

Fix x in X and put c = X.fromSpecStalk x. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism], c is flat, hence so is its pullback g = pullback.snd c U.ι. Put j = pullback.fst c U.ι, an open immersion into Spec O_{X,x}. Apply [lem-a1-local-spectrum-open-classification] to j.opensRange. If it contains the closed point, it is the whole affine spectrum. Otherwise its induced scheme is affine by that classification. The isomorphism from the source of j to its open range therefore makes the source affine in both cases. Since the target is affine, j is an affine morphism.

Let F′ = tensorPullback(g)(F). Uniqueness of left adjoints identifies tensorPullback(g) with the usual module pullback; transport quasi-coherence across this isomorphism. Apply [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi] to the affine morphism j and F′ to obtain H = R^p j_*F′ = 0 for p > 0.

Choose injective resolutions I of F and J of F′. The comparison lift of [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-lift] gives an augmentation-preserving chain map t. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-base-change-resolution-iso], its actual sheaf-valued comparison beta : c*G → H is an isomorphism, since U.ι is quasi-compact and quasi-separated and c and g are flat.

Take the adjoint a : G → c_*H of beta. By [lem-weil-pbc-local-pullback-adjoint-stalk-iso], its map on the stalk at x is invertible. Pushforward and the module-stalk functor preserve the zero object, so H = 0 implies (c_*H)_x = 0. Transport across the stalk isomorphism to conclude G_x = 0. The underlying abelian stalk is therefore subsingleton, proving the stalkwise condition of the first step.
